findings.body: The new picker tests stub `api.ask` and inject a `plantClarification` response directly into jsdom. The repository has no Playwright flow driving a browser through the running API with a real user/database, so this coverage cannot prove that several grants produce the picker before figure reads, a singleton grant answers directly, all ingresses re-check grants, or the selected plants survive the real plant-to-period round trip. The supplied functional-check paragraph also does not identify a running API or database. Done-when item 1 therefore lacks the required real-entry-point test.

findings.body: This table test fabricates each `blocked_by_policy` response through the mocked frontend API. It never exercises request-origin serialization, the running Ask route, grant changes, or the server-selected refusal reason before checking the rendered copy. Although the save/pin portion has separate task evidence, this branch leaves the Ask portion of Done-when item 9 proven only at the component boundary; no required browser/API/database test exists, and the functional-check paragraph does not establish those real boundaries.

findings.body: This change introduces a new styled, scrollable checkbox picker and its validation/loading/error states. The commit records a generic UI checklist and an Emil interaction review, but it does not attest or record impeccable's required shape-before-building pass followed by its audit and polish pass. Run and record that required visual-design review for the changed picker before merging.
findings.title: Not done: impeccable UI pass

findings.body: The picker submits through the generic `"retain"` continuation policy. If this request rejects, `resolveContinueError` in `use-ask.ts:341` displays “The period could not be loaded. Try again.”; a resolved non-success response similarly uses “That period could not be loaded” at `use-ask.ts:312`. At this point the user selected plants and may not have reached a period choice, so the recovery message identifies the wrong failed action. Pass continuation context or use a plant-neutral failure message, and cover the picker failure path.
findings.title: Plant-choice failures are mislabeled as period failures
